I've been farming this land since I was a teenager, watching my father do the same. Here in Quzhou, everyone grows winter wheat and summer maize — that's just what you do. The land is flat, we have the wells for irrigation, and there's always a buyer at harvest. I don't know any other way, and I don't need to. My neighbors grow wheat and maize, the seed seller in town carries the varieties that work here, and I know what to expect from these crops.

I have about 8 mu. After the wheat comes off in June, I'll turn the land and plant maize right after. Same ground, twice a year. That's how my father did it.

For wheat, I use the improved seeds from the county seed shop — not the old varieties, those yield less. For maize I buy hybrid seed, same as everyone. I apply urea and DAP at planting and again when the wheat joints. I irrigate before winter sets in, then again at jointing, then at heading — three times. Two sprays: one for weeds in spring, one for aphids or mildew if it gets bad.

For maize, less rain work to do in summer, but I still run the pump twice — once to get it going, once around tasseling if August is dry. I spray herbicide after seeding and watch for corn borer.

I till with the rotary before wheat planting every autumn. That's how we've always done it.
